MINUTES OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE
  CITY OF PALOS VERDES ESTATES,
  CALIFORNIA

  December 15, 2015

  A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Palos Verdes Estates was
called to order by Chair Thomas at 6:33 p.m. on December 15, 2015, in the City Council
Chambers, 340 Palos Verdes Drive West, Palos Verdes Estates, California. The Pledge of
Allegiance followed.

ROLL CALL

Present:  Kao, Evans, Hunter, Welch, Chair Thomas

Absent:  None

Also Present: Planning Director Sheri Repp-Loadsman; City Planner Elizabeth Corpuz;
  Assistant City Attorney John Cotti; Julie Cremeans, Minutes Secretary

  *  *  *

COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

None.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Chair Thomas, upon confirmation the applicants present understood the suggested conditions of
approval, opened the public hearing, confirmed that there were no interested persons wishing to
voice concerns regarding the application considered for the Consent Calendar, and closed the
public hearing.

1.  M-1072-15; Consideration of a Miscellaneous Application for structures exceeding the
  allowable height within the setback adjacent to the street and non-standard
  encroachments within the City right-of-way at the single family residence located at 3301
  Via La Selva. Lot 1 & a portion of Lot 2, Block 6100, Tract 6883. This project is exempt
  from CEQA pursuant to California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section
  15303.

  Applicant/Owner: Jeff & Michelle Aleixo

Planning Commission  1  December 15, 2015
 2.  M-1069-15; Consideration of a Miscellaneous Application for an accessory structure
  exceeding the allowable height at the single family residence located at 2124 Chelsea
  Road. Lot 1, Block 2102, Tract 7331. This project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to
  California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.

  Applicant:  Deborah Richie-Bray
  2432 Via Amador
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

  Owner:  Kevin & Hilda Buckle

MOTION

  Commissioner Evans moved to approve M-1072-15 for 3301 Via La Selva, exempt from
CEQA and subject to the conditions as provided in Planning Resolution PCR-2015-0897 with
standard conditions and the following additional conditions: 1) a license agreement shall be
submitted to defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the city, its officers, agents and employees
from and against any and all loss, damage, liability, claims, demands, costs, charges, and
expenses, including attorney’s fees, and causes of action of whatsoever character which the City
may incur, sustain or be subjected to on account of loss or damage to property or loss of use
thereof, or for bodily injury to or death of any person arising out of or in any way connected to
the encroachment; and 2) a license agreement shall be submitted to reimburse the City for any
costs incurred by the City to repair damage, restore premises, or satisfy claims incurred by
reason of the encroachment; and M-1069-15 for 2124 Chelsea Road, exempt from CEQA and
subject to the conditions as provided in Planning Resolution PCR-2015-0891 with standard
conditions and the following additional condition: the sewer easement and sewer lines shall be
plotted on the plan to ensure there are no encroachments into the easement or impacts to the
sewer. The motion was seconded by Commissioner Kao and was carried by unanimous oral
vote.

NEW BUSINESS

3.  NC-943RIII/G-1563/M-1073-15; Consideration of a revised Neighborhood
  Compatibility, Grading and Miscellaneous Applications for a new accessory structure at
  the single family residence located at 1341 Via Cataluna. Lot 11, Block 9, Tract 7538.
  This project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to California Administrative Code Title 14,
  Chapter 3, Section 15303.

  Applicant:  Envirotechno Architecture
  27010 Springcreek Rd.
  Rancho Palos Verdes, CA 90275

  Owner:  George & Georgene Mitsanas

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

Commissioner Welch asked about lot coverage and the 5-foot setback, and City Planner Corpuz
explained the Code.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Planning Commission  2  December 15, 2015
 Luis DeMoraes (architect at 27010 Springcreek Road, Rancho Palos Verdes) came forward and
presented the application.

Commissioner Welch asked about lot coverage, and Commissioner Thomas asked about
landscaping Mr. DeMoraes provided the lot coverage data and explained the landscaping plan.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Commissioner Welch commented that it is more a matter of calculation and math than anything
else, and the Commission should avoid setting a precedent to allow someone to increase building
area, cover it and have more massive structures.

Commissioners Evans and Hunter and Chair Thomas concurred.

Commissioner Kao also concurred and added that it is a creative way to achieve the intended
purpose.

MOTION

  Commissioner Hunter moved to approve NC-943RIII/G-1563/M-1073-15 for 1341 Via
Cataluna, exempt from CEQA and subject to the conditions as provided in Planning Resolution
PCR-2015-0895 with standard conditions and the following additional conditions: 1) payment to
the City tree bank shall be required for each street tree approved or required to be removed
within the City right-of-way; 2) the non-standard encroachments, which consists of retaining
walls, shall be terminated at least 5-feet behind the back of curb; 3) a license agreement shall be
submitted to defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the city, its officers, agents and employees
from and against any and all loss, damage, liability, claims, demands, costs, charges, and
expenses, including attorney’s fees, and causes of action of whatsoever character which the City
may incur, sustain or be subjected to on account of loss or damage to property or loss of use
thereof, or for bodily injury to or death of any person arising out of or in any way connected to
the encroachment; and 4) a license agreement shall be submitted to reimburse the City for any
costs incurred by the City to repair damage, restore premises, or satisfy claims incurred by
reason of the encroachment. The motion was seconded by Commissioner Evans and was carried
by unanimous oral vote.

OLD BUSINESS

4.  NC-1526/G-1549-15; Consideration of Neighborhood Compatibility & Grading
  Applications for a new single family residence located at 1304 Palos Verdes Drive West.
  Lot 7, Block 6, Tract 8043. This project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to California
  Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.

  Applicant:  Tomaro Architecture
  2617 N. Sepulveda Blvd., #100
  Manhattan Beach, CA 90266

  Owner:  Lydia & Kevin Tracy

Commissioner Evans advised that he was not here in July but has reviewed the minutes.

Planning Commission  3  December 15, 2015
 City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material, and advised that action
must be taken.

Commissioner Evans asked about the project qualifying as a basement, and City Planner Corpuz
explained that it does meet the basement calculation.

Commissioner Hunter asked for an explanation of those calculations and language, and City
Planner Corpuz demonstrated the calculation and explained the Code. Assistant City Attorney
Cotti added that the Commission can reject the application without prejudice, which would allow
the applicant to come back with a new application.

Commissioner Evans asked about the sewer line easement, and City Planner Corpuz asked that
the Commission condition the application that the sewer lines be showed on the plans.

Commissioner Kao asked about the new project referenced in the neighborhood compatibility
application with respect to scale. City Planner Corpuz advised that the City has not received a
formal application for a new project.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Louie Tomaro (architect at 2617 North Sepulveda Boulevard, Manhattan Beach) came forward
and presented the application.

Commissioner Kao asked about a forthcoming project to the south, and Mr. Tomaro advised that
there was a new project, but that house is now being sold, so that has changed.

Simon Salehi (1300 Palos Verdes Drive West) came forward against the application, pointing out
that the plan is now an L shaped structure looming as a three-story house 25 feet above his
driveway and facing his windows. Mr. Salehi asked that the Commission request that the
applicant design a two-story house.

Mr. Tomaro re-approached and discussed the basement qualification, the elevations and the slope
of the lot, explaining that the house steps with the grade and at no point exceeds 25 feet above
any grade and that a one-story house would be almost under grade toward the back.

Commissioner Welch asked about the natural grade line and calculations, and Mr. Tomaro
explained both.

Commissioner Hunter asked about the north elevation, and Mr. Tomaro discussed that elevation.

Chair Thomas asked about translucent windows on the two-story element on the north side, and
Mr. Tomaro agreed that could be done, as the windows are for ventilation only.

Commissioner Evans asked about the number of bedrooms and bathrooms, and Mr. Tomaro
pointed out the 6 bedrooms and 7½ bathrooms.

Commissioner Kao asked about a reduction in plate heights, and Mr. Tomaro responded that they
can be reduced.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Planning Commission  4  December 15, 2015
 Chair Thomas advised that the technical definition of a basement is immaterial because Staff has
determined its qualification. What matters is whether the application is compatible and sized
properly and the impacts have been mitigated.

Commissioner Welch commented that if it was 1½ feet different it would be a three-story
building and commended the architect for his creativity with the driveway, garage and second
floor to address the concerns presented at the July meeting. If it qualifies as a two-story building
then the issue around compatibility is about size. This is very, very close, and maybe some plate
height conditions could be placed for the three levels.

Commissioner Kao agreed that the architect is very talented and creative with over 5,000 square
feet of the 6,400 square foot living area be contained in the basement and first floor, mitigating
the third level, but it is still looming for the neighbors and drivers. Commissioner Kao asked that
the height be mitigated and that the application be denied without prejudice so that the applicant
can file a new application.

Commissioner Evans commented that the project looks like three-story structure, and
notwithstanding the definition of a basement it’s clear that it looms over the adjacent neighbors
and is way out of scale for the neighborhood in terms of mass and scale. The whole second story
needs to be removed and a house designed within the existing two-story structure.

Commissioner Hunter commented that good progress has been made with the driveway, garage
and parking changes, but the home is clearly large relative to the other homes and looks like a
three-story house. It is at minimum setback on the north side, and putting this massive house at
the bare minimum setback to the neighbor is aggressive.

Chair Thomas commented that he appreciated the changes made responsive to feedback, but it
would not be the right decision to condition this and let it go through. The basement is being
used as a mechanism to create a very large house, the second story impact is concerning, and the
element at the back looks like accessory structures that the Commission sometimes denies. If it
came back with some modifications it would have a good chance of getting through.

Assistant City Attorney Cotti advised that in some cities the same or a similar project can not be
reapplied for within a period of time, but this city does not have that restriction, so a straight
denial would be fine, though the Commission might be able to waive fees. Planning Director
Repp-Loadsman pointed out that this commission has no past practice in denying a project and
having it come back and there is a significant amount of staff and attorney time, so she would
advise being careful about waiving fees, and City Council would need to concur with continuing
and waiving fees. Chair Thomas advised that the Commission not take that approach, as it is
aware of the rules and should follow them.

MOTION

  Commissioner Kao moved to deny without prejudice NC-1526/G-1549-15 for 1304 Palos
Verdes Drive West. The motion was seconded by Commissioner Evans and was carried by
unanimous oral consent.

City Planner Corpuz advised that Staff will prepare a resolution that indicates a denial.

Planning Commission  5  December 15, 2015
 5.  NC-1540/G-1558/M-1051-15; Consideration of Neighborhood Compatibility, Grading,
  & Miscellaneous Applications for a new single family residence located at 908 Via
  Rincon. Lot 9, Block 1630, Tract 7142. This project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to
  California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.

  Applicant:  George Sweeney
  3 Malaga Cove Plaza #201
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

  Owner:  Richard & Cecilia Hu

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

Commissioner Evans asked what hillside residential means, and City Planner Corpuz explained
the requirements, which recently changed in July 2015.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

George Sweeney (3 Malaga Cove Plaza) came forward and presented the application.

Commissioner Evans asked whether 9 trees are being removed, and Mr. Sweeney responded
affirmatively. Commissioner Evans asked about the tree in the center of the picture obscuring
the silhouette, and Mr. Sweeney responded that it would be removed. Commissioner Kao asked
about extrapolating the silhouette of the structure, and Mr. Sweeney advised that it would follow
the contour of the tree to the right, someone lower, maybe 4 or 5 feet.

Ellen Cheng (929 Via Rincon) came forward and asked that the project be reduced to mitigate
the massive and overbearing feeling after removal of the trees.

Susan Booker (933 Via Rincon) came forward and advised that the project will affect her ocean
view and asked that it be moved to the southwest by 18 feet.

Jim Nazemi (932 Via Del Monte) came forward and objected to the project due to his view
obstruction and asked that the project be pulled back by 12 feet.

Mr. Sweeney re-approached and advised that an agreement was reached to remove the solarium
portion of the family room at the main level, not at the upper floor level, and that the demands
and objections are not reasonable. The issue is and should be about the trees.

Cynthia Hu (owner at 908 Via Rincon) came forward and agreed that she promised to remove
the solarium, which she did, and replaced it with a small patio balcony.

Commissioner Welch asked about the 700 square foot terrace on the first floor level, and
Mr. Sweeney responded that it was a terrace at the family room level, but that part of the
structure has been removed, so the first floor structure was replaced by an exterior terrace, as
agreed, with a cantilever balcony three feet deep on the floor above that.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Commissioner Hunter asked about the differences in square footages of the adjacent homes
shown on the applicant’s slide versus shown in the Staff report, and City Planner Corpuz

Planning Commission  6  December 15, 2015
 discussed county tax assessor records showing only livable square footage and not the garage
and advised that applicant has probably gone off of the approved plans from the homes
association.

Commissioner Welch commented that this is a very large project and that the view from the
beach to the hill has changed dramatically on the peninsula from a more pastoral landscape to
very large structures that are now part of what we have in terms of neighborhood compatibility.
There are impacts on views with a structure like this; however, the incredible view is still an
incredible view even with this house. Weighing ownership of this property’s right to build a
project versus what’s being traded off in terms of view, it can be approved as submitted.

Commissioner Hunter commented that there are four unnecessary chimneys that protrude up
quite a bit. It’s a massive house that will stand out on the hillside, but at the end of the day the
owner of the property should be permitted to go forward with the project, and there are a number
of other very large homes in the neighborhood.

Commissioner Kao commented that the applicant has been responsive to the Commission’s
requests to be compatible with neighborhood compatibility and is not obligated to remove the
threes but is just making that concession. There will be a net gain in view for the neighbors, so
with the additional condition that the nine trees be removed, the application can be approved.

Commissioner Evans commented that the residents are rightly concerned about preserving their
spectacular view, and removing the nine trees does that and enhances the view. Removing the
chimneys also makes sense.

Chair Thomas agreed and added that the applicant has made significant strides to improve the
application and that the Commission can’t eliminate all impacts but can only go through the
process to assure that the applicant has mitigated the impacts. With a condition that the gates
and pilasters not exceed allowable height, the application is approvable.

MOTION

  Commissioner Hunter moved to approve NC-1540/G-1558/M-1051-15 for 908 Via
Rincon, exempt from CEQA and subject to the conditions as provided in Planning Resolution
PCR-2015-0849 with standard conditions and the following additional conditions: 1) a standard
urban storm water mitigation plan, approved by the City Engineer shall be prepared and
implemented for the project; 2) this project is considered Hillside Residential and shall comply
with Municipal NPDES Permit; 3) curb and gutter along property frontage with Via Rincon shall
be installed. Engineering and design shall be in accordance with City standards; 4) the sewer
easement and sewer lines shall be plotted on the plan to ensure there are no encroachments into
the easement or impacts to the sewer; 5) the chimneys shall be removed; 6) the Miscellaneous
application related to the fences, gates, and pilasters exceeding the allowable height is denied;
and 7) the nine trees shown to be removed on Sheet 1.1 of the plans shall be removed. The
motion was seconded by Commissioner Kao and was carried by unanimous oral vote.

Planning Commission  7  December 15, 2015
 6.  NC-1543/G-1560/M-1064/M-1065-15; Consideration of Neighborhood Compatibility,
  Grading & Miscellaneous Applications for a new single family residence located at 709
  Via Somonte. Lot 11, Block 1538, Tract 6884. This project is exempt from CEQA
  pursuant to California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.

  Applicant/Owner: GA Design Inc.

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

Commissioner Welch asked whether the curb and gutter requirement has been applied to other
construction on the street, and City Planner Corpuz responded that the standard is to require that
curb and gutter be installed.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Mahmoud Gharachedaghi (architect at GA Design Architecture and Planning, 19191 S. Vermont
Avenue, #640, Torrance) came forward and presented the application.

Commissioner Hunter and Chair Thomas asked about ridge heights, and Mr. Gharachedaghi
explained that the heights came down by more than 2’6”.

Commissioner Welch asked about the Art Jury process, and Mr. Gharachedaghi explained that
the Art Jury approved the first design with minor changes and that the project will be resubmitted
after direction from the Commission.

John Dixon (641 Via Del Monte) came forward and commented that he bought into a planned
community with neighborhood compatibility regulations and that these four to five contiguous
houses were approved at existing ridge elevation because of the nature of Via Somonte, and any
increase in elevation is a violation of the historic approvals of these homes.

Elaine Bohmer (793 Via Somonte) came forward and commented that the revisions to the plans
do not do enough to reduce the view obstruction or overall mass.

Derek Lazzaro (804 Via Somonte) came forward and commented that that further modifications
are necessary and requested a reduction in impact of the view. The overall height in the center
has only gone down 2 feet, and there’s a significant impact on other houses to the side as well as
to the Bohmers. There is also a concern that there will be a domino effect.

Rick Bohmer (793 Via Somonte) came forward and commented that there was not enough
change and also requested that the tree height be limited to the height of the ridgeline.

Steve O’Neil (712 Via Somonte) came forward with concerns of privacy, encroachments,
compatibility in this region and setting a precedent. Putting another level on top of the homes
that are two stories could set a precedent, not only on Via Somonte but Via Del Monte,
impacting views along Via Somonte.

Fred Greogry (816 Via Somonte) came forward with concerns about the shocking view impact,
audaciousness, disregard for neighborhood compatibility, setting a precedent and invasion of
privacy. Mr. Gregory also requested a moratorium on the nonstop construction for many years
on Via Somonte.

Planning Commission  8  December 15, 2015
 Gerry Brooke (812 Via Somonte) came forward and commented that the applicant only made
small changes, and the project is still inappropriate for this parcel.

Stephanie Streisand (705 Via Somonte) came forward in support of the project, stating that it :
does not impact her view or privacy, that these lots are very narrow and steep and difficult to do
a reconstruction project on, that efforts were made to lower the project and lower the first level
of the home, and that the project is for a two-level home, not a three-level.

Mr. Gharachedaghi re-approached and advised that there were several meetings held to hear and
mitigate concerns and changes were made based on the neighbors’ recommendations. It follows
the same style of the neighbors and is smaller than any new building in the area.

Chair Thomas and Mr. Gharachedaghi then discussed consideration of possible alternatives.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Commissioner Evans commented that this area is uniquely suited to the neighborhood
compatibility ordinance. This project fails on at least three counts: neighborhood compatibility,
view impact and overall massing. Modest adjustments were made, but the applicant has not
demonstrated the level of innovation and thinking that will be required to meet neighborhood
compatibility.

Commissioner Kao agreed, adding that the floor area would be 43.3%, the second largest in the
area, with massing and view impacts. There has been improvement, but the application is still a
far cry from approvable.

Commissioner Welch commented that there has been significant improvement from the last
submittal in architectural style and change in roof, but there is clearly an impact from the
Bohmers’ home. The difficulty with this property is that it’s a very small lot. Compared to the
entire queen’s necklace view, this is a reasonable impact, and there is a precedent in the area for
this amount of view obstruction, but privacy impacts should be considered.

Commissioner Hunter agreed that the applicant has made significant improvements in terms of
the impact to neighbors. Looking at natural grade for his property, it is really sunk down on his
first level. It would require a significant complete redesign.

Chair Thomas agreed that there were material changes but not enough to win approval. With a
small lot like this there are some opportunities that have not been exploited. Everything
reasonable and practicable has not been done to mitigate impacts to neighbors, and it needs a
more novel and creative approach.

Mr. Gharachedaghi accepted an extension.

CONTINUED TO THE JANUARY 19, 2016, PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING

Planning Commission  9  December 15, 2015
 7.  M-1067-15; Consideration of a Miscellaneous Application for an accessory structure
  exceeding the allowable height at the single family residence located at 3819 Via La
  Selva. Portion of Lot T, Tract 6887. This project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to
  California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303

  Applicant:  Tomaro Architecture
  2617 N. Sepulveda Blvd., #100
  Manhattan Beach, CA 90266

  Owner:  Javier & Jenna Martinez
  4733 Torrance Blvd., #121
  Torrance, CA 90503

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

Commissioner Welch asked whether the project meets the projected rear yard setback, and City
Planner Corpuz responded that it would be considered nonconforming if approved.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Louie Tomaro (architect at 2617 North Sepulveda Boulevard, Manhattan Beach) came forward
and presented the application.

Commissioner Kao and Mr. Tomaro discussed the reasons for the location, a noise barrier,
privacy and parking.

Commissioner Welch asked the architect to compare the approved structure and the structure
being requested, and Mr. Tomaro provided a comparison.

Tom Funk (3925 Via Picaposte) came forward stating that the project is too large and blocks
sunlight.

Mr. Tomaro re-approached and clarified that there is no continuation of the house, a 10-foot
separation is required between a structure and the main house, and the hip roof wouldn’t impact
much of the light, if any.

Commissioner Kao asked why the new design needs to be so much higher, and Mr. Tomaro
explained the addition of a sloped roof with a wider height. The project previously went down
into the side yard for access but now proposes access from the covered area.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Commissioner Hunter commented that the neighbor only has a fairly narrow window to allow
light to enter the site, and this is a large lot and already has a very large covered patio that has an
even higher 18-foot covered patio only a few feet away from the new proposed covered
structure. It’s a big structure that the neighbor will have to look at, which is not reasonable,
given all the options where it could be placed.

Commissioner Welch commented that the Funk house is a massive house for its lot. There has
been mitigation, but this wasn’t an easy plan to approve because of the level of development on
